items.title: Copy here, paste there
items.detail: While you control another computer, what you copy on one can be pasted on the other: text and pictures. Passwords from password managers stay on the computer they were copied on. Turn it off in Settings → Clipboard and files.

items.title: Send files by dragging them
items.detail: Drag files or folders onto the window showing the other computer. They arrive in its Downloads folder, exactly as sent.

items.title: Drop files at the top of the screen
items.detail: Start dragging a file and a silver island pops out at the top of the screen (from the notch on a Mac). Bring the file close and drop it there to send it. Files coming in show there too.

items.title: Scrolling feels the same everywhere
items.detail: A Mac controlling Windows or Linux now scrolls the same way it does on the Mac. Change it in Settings → Viewing.

items.title: A log that explains what went wrong
items.detail: Settings → Developer → Show log files. When something fails, the moments before it are saved in the crashes folder. Turn on Verbose logging while chasing a problem. Only your account can read the log, and it never holds what you type, copy or send.

items.title: Smoother scrolling on a Mac you control
Linux Extend matches the viewer's screen
items.detail: The extra display uses the viewer's scale, so text is the right size. Change it in Settings.

items.title: Annex on a Mac no longer opens Tailscale
items.detail: Looking for nearby computers no longer starts the Tailscale app.
